#!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 #1267,
# AC-1.2/AC-1.3; SDD §5.3). check-loa.sh check_integrity classifies every
# manifest path as ok, Tampered (fail), not-mounted (a submodule mount does
# not link it but .loa/<path> has it: counted, one summary line, never a
# failure) or Missing (fail).
#
# Seam: check-loa.sh already guards `main` behind
#   [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]
# so each case sources the script in a child bash inside the fixture
# directory and calls check_integrity alone; the child exits 1 when the
# FAILURES counter is non-zero, the same rule main applies. No other check
# runs, and the script is not modified for the test.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
  CHECK="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cloams.XXXXXX")"
  D="$T/downstream"
  # upstream tree inside the submodule path
  mkdir -p "$D/.loa/.claude/lib" "$D/.claude"
  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh"
  printf 'echo b\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh"
  printf 'echo c\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh"
  # the mount links a.sh only (b.sh and lib/c.sh are not linked)
  ln -s ../.loa/.claude/a.sh "$D/.claude/a.sh"
  printf 'aleph:\n  enabled: false\n' > "$D/.loa.config.yaml"
  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
  HA="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  HB="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  HC="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  write_manifest
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# write_manifest [extra-path hash]... — a/b/lib/c plus any extra pairs
write_manifest() {
  local args=(--arg a "$HA" --arg b "$HB" --arg c "$HC")
  local filter='{".claude/a.sh": $a, ".claude/b.sh": $b, ".claude/lib/c.sh": $c}'
  if [[ $# -ge 2 ]]; then
    args+=(--arg xp "$1" --arg xh "$2")
    filter="$filter + {(\$xp): \$xh}"
  fi
  jq -n "${args[@]}" "{generated: \"2026-10-15T00:00:00Z\", algorithm: \"sha256\", files: ($filter)}" \
    > "$D/.claude/checksums.json"
}

run_integrity() {
  run bash -c 'cd "$1" && source "$2" && check_integrity && echo "FAILURES=$FAILURES" && [[ $FAILURES -eq 0 ]]' \
    _ "$D" "$CHECK"
}

@test "CM-1 paths in the upstream tree but not linked are not-mounted; exit unaffected" {
  run_integrity
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"not-mounted: 2 path(s) exist in the upstream tree but are not linked by this mount"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"Integrity verified"* ]]
167

[[ -n "$effort" ]] && argv+=(--effort "$effort")

events="$eval_dir/events.jsonl"
stderr_log="$eval_dir/agent-stderr.log"
start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
rc=0
(
  cd "$WORKSPACE" || exit 2
  export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH="$eval_dir/model-invoke.jsonl"
  export LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH="$eval_dir/cost-ledger.jsonl"
  export EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL"
  # sprint-237 audit HIGH-001: the CLI keeps HOME (its own credentials live there)
  # and PATH (its toolchain); the operator's other credentials are not the agent
  # under test's business, and its temp files stay inside the sandbox.
  unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
  # cycle-129: an executor started from inside a Claude Code session inherits
  # that session's coupling (child-session flag, session id, messaging socket,
  # agent teams) and its subagent model (the sprint-255 driver session carried
  # CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=opus). Decouple the session and pin every
  # auxiliary model to the executor model. (A safeguard-refusal fallback to
  # another model is a separate CLI behaviour, recorded below as
  # refusal_fallbacks; no environment setting turns it off.)
  unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET \
    CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED
  export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="$MODEL"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir/tmp" && export TMPDIR="$eval_dir/tmp"
  exec timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$TIMEOUT_S" "${argv[@]}"
) > "$events" 2> "$stderr_log" || rc=$?
end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
duration_ms=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))

# --- 4. record ---------------------------------------------------------------
# The last `result` event is the CLI's summary (absent on crash/timeout).
result_json="$(grep -E '^\{.*"type" *: *"result"' "$events" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
if [[ -z "$result_json" ]] || ! jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$result_json"; then
  result_json='{"type":"result","subtype":"missing","is_error":true}'
fi
printf '%s\n' "$result_json" > "$eval_dir/agent-output.json"

# Ordered tool writes from the transcript (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit).
tool_writes="$(jq -c '
  select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]? |

  unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN

  # agent teams) and its subagent model (the sprint-255 driver session carried

head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:178 — The new integrity gate (`check-manifest-paths.sh` + `gen-checksums.sh --check`) is added, but the PR does not regenerate `.claude/checksums.json`. The same PR edits tracked `.claude/` files: `defaults/model-config.yaml`, `loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`, `scripts/check-loa.sh`, `scripts/preflight.sh`, `scripts/generated-model-maps.sh`, the bridgebuilder `dist/` and `resources/` generated files, and `adapters/tests/test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py`. So `--check` reports every one of them as `changed` and CI fails on this PR. If merged, downstream `check-loa.sh` reports those files as Tampered, which is the #1267 symptom this sprint is meant to fix. Also, the manifest now in the repo was made by the legacy `find` walker, so `check-manifest-paths.sh` may reject it too. Run `bash tools/gen-checksums.sh` and commit the result.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:386 — Trust-boundary break. `regen_sandbox_manifest` runs `${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE}/tools/gen-checksums.sh`. That is the pinned or PR tree under evaluation (run-arms passes the source worktree as `EVAL_PROMPT_TREE`), and the script sources that tree's `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`. So code from the tree under test runs in the trusted harness. This contradicts the library's own contract at lines 75 and 96-100 ("Hashing is Python hashlib, never .claude/ code") and eval.yml's "Validate grader trust boundary". Always use the inline hashlib path, or only the harness's own copy.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:221 — The sandbox manifest is regenerated for every arm-mode run, including `baseline` and the cycle-129 recall arms (run-arms.sh always sets `LOA_EVAL_ARM`). Every cycle-129 single-skill sandbox now gains a `.claude/checksums.json` the agent can read, and `arm_evidence` gains `manifest_files` and `manifest_sha256`. This contradicts the "WITHOUT behaviour change for the cycle-129 single-skill path" claim (sandbox-mount.sh:6-7) and makes new recall batches incomparable with earlier ones. Limit it to arms whose toggles actually edit `.claude/`, or to the pipeline executor.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:131 — The tree mount uses `cp -a`, which keeps symlinks as symlinks, but the contract (line 18) promises "files, never a symlink to the tree". A source tree laid out as a submodule mount (`.claude/*` linking into `.loa/`, the #1267 layout) gives the sandbox dangling links, or absolute links to host paths, which also reach the container through the `/workspace` bind mount. Dereference the links (`cp -RL`, or `cp -aL`).
head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75 — In a submodule mount, any manifest path that is missing under `.claude/` but present under `.loa/` is now counted as not-mounted and never fails. Upstream always has every path, so deleting a file or symlink the mount does link (a hook, a script) is no longer reported as Missing. The integrity check can no longer detect removal of mounted files. Classify against the set of paths the mount actually links, not against what exists upstream.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:20 — Dead build stage. `brbuild` runs `cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6`, but line 82 says that version is not on crates.io, and no stage copies from `brbuild`. BuildKit skips the stage; the legacy builder (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`) builds every stage, so the documented `docker build` fails. It also pulls an unpinned `rust:1-bookworm`. Remove the stage.
head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:25 — `CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1` contradicts pipeline-run.sh:85 ("codex 0.137.0 by Dockerfile.ablation"). The header that tells readers which toolchain versions a batch ran on is wrong, and that matters because `image_digest` is meant to identify the batch's versions.
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:506 — The arm-id leak guard is an unbounded substring grep over the whole sandbox, including the copied `.claude/` tree and the review-catch `pr/` copy. The hidden-path guard above it prunes `.claude`; this one does not. Any review-catch fixture whose diff mentions an arm id (for example, a PR touching `evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml`) becomes an `infrastructure_error` and can never run. Scope the guard to the fixture and grimoire paths the harness wrote, and match on word boundaries as validate-suite.sh does.
head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:87 — Rule evidence such as `one_voice_planned` is read from `sandbox/grimoires/.../adversarial-*.json` first. That is an agent-writable file, preferred over the driver's `eval/` copy, even though the header (line 10) promises evidence "never from what the agent said". ablation-row.sh:201 does the same for `voices_run` and `degraded`. Prefer the `eval/` copy the driver captured after each phase.
head/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh:54 — The bats fallback is a hard-coded path from one operator's dotfiles (`~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats`). On any other host this changes the fingerprint to `bats=absent` instead of finding the tool. Use `bats` on PATH or `--bats-bin` / `LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN` only.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

The review is in `/workspace/review.md` with 10 findings and the verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I read the diff and the head files closely but ran nothing: no bats suite and no `gen-checksums.sh --check`, because `compat-lib.sh` isn't in the frozen tree.

**Blocking:**
1. **CI will fail on this PR.** It adds the `gen-checksums.sh --check` and `check-manifest-paths.sh` gate (`.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:178`). But it edits about a dozen tracked `.claude/` files and never regenerates `.claude/checksums.json`. The check will flag every one of those files as changed. Merged as is, downstream `check-loa.sh` would report them as Tampered, which is the #1267 problem this sprint is meant to fix. I worked this out from the file list, not by running the check.
2. **Trust-boundary break** (`lib/sandbox-mount.sh:386`). Rebuilding the sandbox manifest can run `tools/gen-checksums.sh` from the tree being evaluated. That script loads the tree's own `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`, so untrusted code runs inside the trusted harness. The library's own header says it never does this. It only happens when the sandbox is a git repo that tracks `.claude/` files.
3. **Unannounced behaviour change for cycle-129 runs** (`execute-agent.sh:221`). Every arm-mode run, including `baseline` and all recall arms, now gets a `.claude/checksums.json` in the sandbox and two extra evidence keys. That contradicts the "no behaviour change" claim and makes new recall batches hard to compare with older ones.

**Other findings:**
- **Symlinks:** `cp -a` copies symlinks as symlinks in the full-tree mount, though the contract promises plain files. A submodule-style source tree leaves dangling links in the sandbox.
